Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking through the assistant use case and sharing the sample prompts. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

- Model recommendations (based on your latency and hallucination tolerance):
  • Primary: Llama-2-13b-chat — good balance of quality for instruction-following and cost.
  • Alternative (low-latency): Mistral-7B-Instruct — lower p99 latency, slightly different failure mode.
  • Edge/embedded evals: Redwood-Instruct-3B-quant (quantized) for POC throughput tests.

- What we’ll share today: Redwood-verified benchmark profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) on your prompt set, and a short POSH (proof-of-service) benchmark report. Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (the prompts you shared) — we used this to run the evals.

- Ask from you: any additional evaluation constraints (hard p99 latency target, max cost/token) and confirmation on which routes we should prioritize (hosted API vs dedicated pool).

I’ve cc’d Marissa from our MLE team — she’ll call out any quality/regression considerations and help interpret the results. Next step: I’ll send the benchmark links and a short mutual action plan.

Subject: Re: Model fit & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme — next steps

Tom — thanks, great questions. Quick answers + links below, plus an appended short benchmark summary.

1) Latency SLOs (single-turn, median length ~60 tokens) — Redwood-hosted (us-west region):
   • Llama-2-13b-chat: p50 ~ 75ms, p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 320ms — meets your targets in our standard hosted configuration.
   • Mistral-7B-Instruct: p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 110ms, p99 ~ 240ms — better tail latency, lower cost per token.
   • Redwood-Instruct-3B-quant: p50 ~ 35ms, p95 ~ 95ms, p99 ~ 170ms — great for high-throughput but watch for mild quality regressions on long-form completions.

2) Throughput (sustained interactive, us-west, single model pool):
   • Llama-2-13b-chat: ~18–22 TPS per GPU under our continuous-batching runtime (depends on avg length and batch window).
   • Mistral-7B-Instruct: ~30–40 TPS per GPU.
   • For your expected burst to 35 TPS we recommend either:
     - Hosted: attach autoscaling + burst capacity (we can provision extra GPU capacity automatically), or
     - Dedicated: 1x dedicated GPU pool (2x Mistral-7B instances) to give headroom and predictable tail latency.

3) Cost delta (rough, hosted list rates):
   • Llama-2-13b-chat: ~$1.10 per 1M input+output tokens (est).
   • Mistral-7B-Instruct: ~$0.55 per 1M tokens.
   • Redwood-Instruct-3B-quant: ~$0.30 per 1M tokens.

Benchmark links / artifacts:
- Redwood-verified benchmark profile (Acme prompt set): https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026-05
- Full POSH report (PDF): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X_example_redwood_bench_acme
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/98765

Attachment: redwood-bench-acme-report.pdf (summary, includes p50/p95/p99 tables and per-model confusion/QA metrics).

Next steps (proposed):
- Alex to schedule a 30m technical demo with Marissa and Dylan to walk the evals and go over regression monitoring (this week).
- Acme to confirm SLOs and preferred deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).
- Redwood to provide a short mutual action plan + NDA/procurement templates if needed.

I’ve attached the report and a mutual action plan draft (MAP-Mutual-Action-Plan.pdf). Marissa — can you call out any red flags re: quality regressions on the prompt set? Dylan — can you advise on expected GPU sizing for a dedicated pool if they go that route?

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-bench-acme-report.pdf, MAP-Mutual-Action-Plan.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Model fit & Redwood-verified benchmarks for Acme — next steps

Hey Tom — quick notes from the evals I ran against acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl: 

- Quality/regression: Llama-2-13b-chat shows higher faithfulness on instruction-following prompts, but we saw ~3.2% higher token-level hallucination on long multi-step instructions vs Mistral-7B. If your flows are multi-step, we recommend Llama-2-13b-chat for quality-sensitive routes and Mistral-7B for short interactive queries.
- Prompt tuning: small prompt engineering (context trimming + explicit system prompt) reduced incorrect completions by ~18% in our tests. We can share sanitized prompt templates.
- Regression monitoring: we recommend integrating our quality monitoring hook to surface prompt-set regressions (we’ll provide a baseline eval set and traffic-based sampling).

I’ll be at the technical demo — happy to walk the failure cases and recommended prompt edits. For dedicated sizing: Dylan — two A10/GPU-equivalent nodes running Mistral-7B should cover steady 35 TPS with 1.5x headroom (we’ll provide a detailed estimate in the MAP).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior MLE, Redwood Inference
